claim_boundary: This is a symbolic reduction for the ordinary separated presentation only. It does not evaluate the Yasui braid presentation and does not prove any exotic-pair separation.

consequence.boring_nontriviality: If the relevant invertible twists are nontrivial, the ordinary split value changes only by the pointed-sector phase theta(g_h)^-1 theta(g_e1) theta(g_e2).
consequence.elimination_rule: A modular category is trivial for this cheap split-link character test whenever every relevant invertible object has twist 1, or more generally whenever theta(g_h)^-1 theta(g_e1) theta(g_e2)=1 for every character assignment under consideration.
what_disappears: non-pointed simple objects except through the baseline Gauss sums

D(A4)_c3w1.interpretation: The Z/3 character directions seen in the ordinary split presentation are represented by bosonic pure-charge invertibles, so every CP2#2CPbar split character twist remains at the baseline value 1728.

Drinfeld_centers.interpretation: Being a center forces total central charge 1, but the split character test is governed by twists of invertible objects. Untwisted doubles with only bosonic relevant invertibles are eliminated; doubles with nontrivial pointed metric can show only pointed-sector phases.

SU2_k.rule: The nontrivial character is parity and is represented by the invertible simple object k, whose twist is exp(pi*i*k/2). Levels k=0 mod 4 are eliminated; all other levels have some nonbaseline split character twist.

Uq_g_general.interpretation: For semisimple quantum-group modular categories, this cheap split test depends only on the simple-current pointed subcategory and its quadratic form. If the simple-current quadratic form is trivial on the relevant subgroup, the test is eliminated; if not, the signal is only a simple-current phase.

proof_sketch.factorization: For a split unlink, the colored Kirby sum factorizes over components.
proof_sketch.single_component_sum: For framing f=+1 or -1 and character chi_g represented by an invertible object g, define tau_f(chi_g)=sum_X d_X^2 chi_g(|X|) theta_X^f.
proof_sketch.balancing_input: In a modular category, chi_g(|X|)=S_{g,X}/d_X is the monodromy character associated to g.
proof_sketch.ratio_formula: For unitary modular data, tau_+1(chi_g)=theta_g^-1 tau_+1(1) and tau_-1(chi_g)=theta_g tau_-1(1).
proof_sketch.split_ratio: Therefore CP2#2CPbar with framings (+1,-1,-1) has ratio theta(g_h)^-1 theta(g_e1) theta(g_e2).
